title: The Street Food Queue
story:
Aisha and her brother Dev arrived at the night market just after seven. A long queue already curled around the busiest stall. The sign above it promised fried noodles with vegetables, egg, and a choice of sauce. They joined the line and moved forward a little at a time.

The vendor worked quickly behind a hot pan. When people asked for a spicy sauce, he pointed to a red bottle and raised his eyebrows. Aisha chose the mild sauce because she had a sore throat. Dev asked for the hotter one and added extra beans. Each portion came in a paper box with a wooden fork.

While they waited, rain began to fall in light drops. A woman shared her umbrella with the child in front of her. Dev pulled up his hood and kept their place. After twenty minutes they reached the counter. Aisha paid for both boxes and said thank you. The vendor nodded and turned back to the pan. The queue behind them was still long. They found a dry step under a shop awning and opened the boxes. Steam rose into the cool air. Aisha's noodles were salty, sweet, and easy to eat. Dev's portion made him reach for water, and he laughed at his own choice. They traded one bite so each could taste the other sauce. Then they stayed a little longer and watched the market lights shine on the wet street.
